place_name: Hozomeen Mountain (North and South Peaks), Ross Lake, North Cascades NP
summit_or_glacier: summit finish (South Peak 8,003 ft); routes are named for the North and South Peaks

evidence.fact: South Peak 8,003 ft via Hozomeen Lake trailhead; round trip 12 miles; the climb to the summit took much of the day.

note: Not on Mountain Project, so route types stay null. No page states a car-to-base time; the verdict rests on the summit finish of a remote peak at the north end of Ross Lake.

place_name: Northwest Mox Peak (Twin Spires), Chilliwack Range
summit_or_glacier: glacier crossing and summit finish

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Snow, Alpine. Scramble class 3/4 to summit; the glacier is quite crevassy, especially on the direct route from the lake.

note: Mountain Project page is the Northeast Ridge of NW Mox (contrasted with the SE Spire). No car-to-base time stated.

place_name: Southeast Mox Peak (Hard Mox), Chilliwack Range
summit_or_glacier: summit finish (Southeast Spire, the summit of Hard Mox)

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Alpine, 3 pitches. Southeast Spire (the summit of Hard Mox); Beckey: one of the most difficult summits in the Cascades.
West ridge first climbed by Fred and Helmy Beckey, 1941; described as a big alpine wall peak.

note: No car-to-base time stated; summit finish decides.

place_name: Sharkfin Tower, Boston Basin
summit_or_glacier: Quien Sabe Glacier approach; summit finish

evidence.fact: From Boston Basin, follow the approach for the Quien Sabe Glacier on Sahale; a gully leads from the glacier to a terrace.
Type: Trad, Snow, Alpine. Final exposed 15 feet to the summit.

note: Glacier approach and summit finish; no car-to-base time stated.

place_name: Cascade Peak (7,428 ft), above Cascade Pass
summit_or_glacier: summit peak; glacier remnants on the north side; standard route is glacier travel plus class 3-4

evidence.fact: Summit 7,428 ft above Cascade Pass; small glacier remnants on the north side; easiest route is glacier travel and class 3-4 scramble.

note: Northwest Chimney is not on Mountain Project, so type null. No car-to-base time stated; summit and glacier decide.

place_name: Crater Crag on Crater Mountain (Canyon Creek trailhead, Hwy 20)
summit_or_glacier: none for the crag itself; it sits at a trail switchback below the summit

evidence.fact: From Canyon Creek trailhead, trails 754/738/746 past Crater Lake to a switchback at ~6320 ft; crag 50 ft above. 6 miles, 4400 ft gain.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 40 ft.

note: Only a distance and gain are stated (6 miles, 4,400 ft), no time; not converted, per the rules. Very likely well over an hour, but no page says so.

place_name: Early Morning Spire, Eldorado Peak area
summit_or_glacier: Inspiration and McAllister Glaciers on the approach

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Snow, Alpine. Approach from Eldorado Creek and the Inspiration Glacier, cross the McAllister Glacier.
Eldorado summit guarded by a long, strenuous approach; probably best done as a 2-3 day climb.

note: Southwest Face is the only route listed under MP's Early Morning Spire area.

place_name: Mix-up Peak, Cascade Pass area
summit_or_glacier: Cache Glacier on the approach; climbing ends near the summit

evidence.fact: When you reach the Cache Glacier aim for the V-Notch gully; the climbing starts about 100 ft below the summit.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 450 ft. Leave the trail just before it drops to the Cache Glacier.

note: Glacier-side approach and summit finish; no car-to-base time stated.

place_name: Mount Chaval, Darrington / Suiattle area
approach_stated: camp set up "8.5 hours from the car"
summit_or_glacier: small glacier on the NE side; snow slopes; summit

evidence.fact: Party set up camp 8.5 hours from the car; failed on the North Ridge; small glacier on Chaval's northeast side.

note: Not on Mountain Project; route type null.

place_name: The Triad, between Eldorado Peak and Hidden Lake Peaks
approach_stated: "scrambled together to the true summit at 11:15am, 6 hours after leaving the car"
summit_or_glacier: glacier travel (crampons) and summit

evidence.fact: Reached the true summit 6 hours after leaving the car; descended to the glacier with crampons and axes.

note: The Mountain Project 'Triad' area found by search is an unrelated crag; the traverse route is not on MP, so type null.

place_name: Davis Peak (7,051 ft), outlier of the Southern Pickets above Diablo
summit_or_glacier: route tops out near the summit

evidence.fact: Burdo and Cairns made a difficult approach to the northern cirque; topped out near the summit.
The steep incline rises 6000 ft in three miles; summit 7,051 ft.

note: Not on Mountain Project; type null. No time stated; summit finish decides.

place_name: Spectre Peak, Northern Pickets
summit_or_glacier: route ends with a long ridge traverse to the summit; snow on the descent

evidence.fact: Haunted Wall (IV 5.9+): round trip 50 miles of hiking and 20,000 ft gain via Easy Ridge; long ridge traverse to summit.

note: Not on Mountain Project; type null. Roadless multi-day backcountry.

place_name: East Twin Needle (7,840 ft), Southern Pickets
approach_stated: "Beginning the 5-hr descent back to the car on Day 3"
summit_or_glacier: summit; steep snow and ice on the Twin Needles

evidence.fact: Tagged both summits (East 7,840 ft); Thread of Gneiss attempted in 2007; 5-hr descent back to the car on day 3.

note: The quoted time is the walk OUT, not in; the verdict rests on the summit finish and multi-day access. Not on Mountain Project; type null.

place_name: Pyramid Peak (The Pyramid, ~8,000 ft), Southern Pickets
summit_or_glacier: summit peak

evidence.fact: A peak in the Southern Pickets north of Inspiration; approach via Goodell Creek or Big Beaver Creek and Ross Lake.
Pyramid Peak 8000 ft; party soloed the south side to the summit, bypassing the 5.8 chimney.

note: MP Pyramid Peak lists no routes, so East Ridge type null. The MP 'The Pyramid' found by search is an unrelated High Desert crag.

place_name: Molar Tooth (7,547 ft), Cutthroat Lake drainage, Washington Pass
summit_or_glacier: summit peak

evidence.fact: Molar Tooth is a 7547 ft summit between Cutthroat Peak and Cutthroat Pass; approaches via PCT from Rainy Pass or Cutthroat Lake trailhead.

note: MP lists only 'North Ridge - West Side'; NE Arete and NE Chimney are not on MP, so types null. No time stated; summit decides.

place_name: Cutthroat Peak, Washington Pass
summit_or_glacier: route ends on the summit

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Alpine, 850 ft. A great way to get to the summit of Cutthroat via the large, steep East Face.

note: No car-to-base time stated; summit finish decides.

place_name: Golden Horn, near Rainy Pass / PCT
summit_or_glacier: summit peak

evidence.fact: Remote granite peak; Northeast Arete 5.8 (Skoog and Walseth 1979) named in the description, not as a route page.
Day trip total time 12 hours 24 minutes; party checked they were on the true summit.

note: NE Arete has no MP route page; type null. No car-to-base time stated.

place_name: Half Moon (Hai Tower), Kangaroo Ridge
summit_or_glacier: route on Hai Tower, the right-most summit of Half Moon

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Alpine, 5 pitches. On Hai Tower, the right-most summit of Half Moon as seen from the highway.
One of the more difficult pinnacles to overcome on Kangaroo Ridge; Getting There: same as the others.

note: No time stated; summit pinnacle decides.

place_name: Liberty Bell Mountain, Washington Pass
summit_or_glacier: summit (7,720 ft)

evidence.fact: Northern summit of the Liberty Bell massif, 7720 ft; park at Blue Lakes trailhead or the east-side overlook; all 19 routes Trad, Alpine.

note: The Barber Pole is not among MP's 19 Liberty Bell routes; type null. The neighbouring NEWS page states 1-2 hours for the approach.

place_name: North Early Winters Spire, Washington Pass
approach_stated: "The approach will take most parties 1-2 hours."
summit_or_glacier: summit (7,760 ft)

evidence.fact: The summit is at 7760 ft. The approach will take most parties 1-2 hours.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 500 ft.

note: Christianson-Roskelley, Twitch of the Death Nerve and Vulcan Death Grip are not listed under MP's NEWS area; types null.

place_name: South Early Winters Spire, Washington Pass
approach_stated: "Blue Lake Trail - ~1 hour of hiking on the trail leads to a meadow and opening on the NW side of the spire"
summit_or_glacier: summit (7,807 ft, highest of the Liberty Bell Group)

evidence.fact: Highest summit of the Liberty Bell Group, 7807 ft; ~1 hour of hiking on the trail leads to a meadow on the NW side.
Neighbouring spire: the approach will take most parties 1-2 hours.

note: The ~1 hour reaches only the meadow, not the base, and the routes are on a summit spire. All three routes are typed Trad, Alpine on their MP pages.

place_name: Poster Peak, Washington Pass (from the Hwy 20 hairpin)
approach_stated: "with a one-hour approach" (stated for Blue's Buttress; House Buttress uses the same approach)
summit_or_glacier: route works up to the top; descent drops off the peak's southwest ridge and a couloir

evidence.fact: Blue Buttress has a one-hour approach; approach House Buttress the same way. To descend the peak, drop off the short southwest ridge.
From the Hairpin, wander SE through the rock field to cairns; a peak offering a couple of alpine routes.

note: The approach is about one hour (borderline crag), but the route ends on the peak and descends from it: a summit finish. House Buttress is not on MP (only Blue's Buttress); type null.

place_name: Burgundy Spire, Wine Spires, Washington Pass
summit_or_glacier: Corkscrew exits into a 400 ft snow couloir (to 50 degrees); summit spire

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Alpine. 8-10 pitches to 5.6 exiting into a 400 ft couloir up to 50 degrees with snow.
Reputedly one of the hardest summits to reach in the Cascades; trail from the Hwy 20 pullout to Burgundy Col.

note: No time stated; snow couloir and summit decide.

place_name: Juno Tower, Vasiliki Ridge, Washington Pass
approach_stated: "Get to base of route (=2:42 for approach)"
summit_or_glacier: summit reached at the end of the climb

evidence.fact: Reached base of route 7:40 am, 2:42 for approach; arrived on summit 3:12 pm.
Zool Patch, listed under MP Juno Tower; Type: Trad, Alpine, 350 ft.

note: The approach time is to the Clean Break (east face) base on the same tower.

place_name: Silver Star Mountain, Washington Pass
summit_or_glacier: glacier route to the summit; largest mountain at Washington Pass

evidence.fact: Largest mountain at Washington Pass; common glacier route with 4th/low 5th scrambling to the summit; approach from milepost 166.

note: MP lists East Ridge, Silver Star Glacier and West Face Couloir only, so Northeast Ridge type null (the MP 'Northeast Ridge' found by search is on Sharkstooth, Colorado).

place_name: Apex Mountain (8,302 ft), Pasayten Wilderness
summit_or_glacier: roadless backcountry; north face above Tungsten Lake cirque

evidence.fact: From Thirtymile Trailhead via Tungsten Trail: Apex Pass at mile 16.0, 4600 ft gained.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 7 pitches, Grade II; north face of Apex above the Tungsten Lake cirque.

note: Roadless wilderness, about 16 trail miles in; no time stated.

place_name: Mount Olympus (West Peak), Olympic National Park
approach_stated: "Typically done over 3 or 4 days. On day 1, hike into Glacier Meadows."
summit_or_glacier: Blue Glacier; summit

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Snow, Alpine. Typically done over 3 or 4 days; day 1 hike into Glacier Meadows; day 2 is summit day.
Travel out the Hoh River Trail to Glacier Meadows for 17.5 miles, then onto the Blue Glacier.

place_name: Grand Teton, Grand Teton National Park
summit_or_glacier: summit; approach from Lupine Meadows via Garnet Canyon to the Lower Saddle

evidence.fact: Most approaches start from Lupine Meadows trailhead into Garnet Canyon, eventually reaching the Lower Saddle.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 1000 ft; scrambling to the summit; Underhill ridge at about 12,900 ft.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 700 ft, 5 pitches, Grade IV.

note: No car-to-base time stated; the high summit decides.

place_name: Medicine Bow Peak east-face slabs (The Diamond), Snowy Range
summit_or_glacier: no summit finish (walk off south to the Medicine Bow Peak trail); seasonal snow: crampons and ice axe useful to reach the base until July

evidence.fact: Shortest approach from Lake Marie recreation area; climbs start above treeline ~10,500 ft; until July crampons and ice axe useful to reach the base.
Approach from Lake Marie described as a short but cross-country trek; no minutes given.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 100 ft.

note: Every page calls the approach short, but none gives minutes. Seasonal snow on the approach until July. theCrag area page has no approach text; SummitPost skipped (403).
